old: The adjectives (sadāhaśūlam ... saraktam) are taken as agreeing with kapham. upaviśati is literally 'sits down'; rendered 'passes' (Hindi 'निकालता है') as the idiomatic sense; the alternative is a looser 'sits and discharges'.
new: The adjectives (sadāhaśūlam ... saraktam) are taken as agreeing with kapham. upaviśati is literally 'sits down'; rendered 'passes' (Hindi 'निकालता है') as the idiomatic sense; the alternative is a looser 'sits and discharges'. The subject 'the patient' is supplied from context (the person of units 38-39); pravahamānaḥ is a bare nominative participle.
why: reviewer (minor): Both translations supply a subject ('the patient' / रोगी); pravahamānaḥ is a bare nominative participle and no noun is printed in this unit. Not recorded in notes.

old: parisrava is kept as the text's term (glossary: flow, trickling); the procedure it refers to is not stated in this line.
new: parisrava is kept as the text's term (literally 'flowing round, oozing'; not yet in the glossary, which fixes only praseka as 'flow, trickling'); the procedure it refers to is not stated in this line.

old: औषध पिए हुए व्यक्ति में औषध, डकार, वमन आदि को रोकने से वात आदि कुपित होकर हृदय का आश्रय लेकर भयंकर हृद्ग्रह ले आते हैं।
new: औषध पिए हुए व्यक्ति में औषध, डकार, छर्दि आदि को रोकने से वात आदि कुपित होकर हृदय का आश्रय लेकर भयंकर हृद्ग्रह ले आते हैं।
why: reviewer (minor): chardi is rendered 'वमन' in Hindi, which conflates it with vamana (the treatment) used in units 45, 58, 67. English keeps them apart (vomiting vs vomiting-treatment). Unit 60 uses छर्दि for chardi.

old: Then, from the affliction of the chief vital spot (marma), the patient is tormented excessively by pains; joined with stupor, hikkā, kāsa (cough), saliva and pain in the side, trembling, with lost consciousness, gnashing his teeth, with eyes turned up, he bites his tongue.
new: Then, from the affliction of the chief vital spot (marma), the patient is tormented excessively by pains; joined with bewilderment, hikkā (hiccup), kāsa (cough), saliva and pain in the side, trembling, with lost consciousness, gnashing his teeth, with eyes turned up, he bites his tongue.
why: reviewer (minor): moha is rendered 'stupor' (a clinical word) here but the verb of the same root in unit 44 (amuhyan) is 'not bewildered'. The plain literal sense is 'bewilderment'. Also kāsa is glossed '(cough)' but hikkā is not, so the glossing is uneven.

old: joined with stupor, hikkā, kāsa, saliva, side-pain
new: joined with bewilderment, hikkā, kāsa, saliva, side-pain
why: reviewer (minor): Gloss uses 'stupor' (see above).

old: तब प्रधान मर्म के उपताप से रोगी वेदनाओं से अत्यन्त पीड़ित होता है; मोह, हिक्का, कास, लाला और पार्श्वशूल से युक्त, काँपता हुआ, संज्ञा खोया हुआ, दाँतों को कटकटाता हुआ, चढ़ी हुई आँखों वाला होकर जीभ को काटता है।
new: तब प्रधान मर्म के उपताप से रोगी वेदनाओं से अत्यन्त पीड़ित होता है; मोह, हिक्का, कास, लाला और पार्श्वशूल से युक्त, काँपता हुआ, संज्ञाहीन, दाँतों को कटकटाता हुआ, चढ़ी हुई आँखों वाला होकर जीभ को काटता है।
why: reviewer (minor): Ungrammatical Hindi ('संज्ञा' is feminine, so 'खोया हुआ' does not agree; the phrase is not standard).

old: tat-puruṣa, m. inst. sg.
new: tat-puruṣa, n. inst. sg. (agrees with taṃdula-aṃbunā)
why: reviewer (minor): Labelled m. inst. sg., but it agrees with taṃdula-aṃbunā (ambu is neuter), so n. inst. sg.

old: तब दोष के शेष को पाचनीय द्रव्यों से पकाए और दोष की उभार के अनुसार बस्तियाँ दे।
new: तब दोष के शेष को पाचनीय द्रव्यों से पकाए और दोष के उभार के अनुसार बस्तियाँ दे।

old: twisting, cramping
new: twisting, wrapping round
why: reviewer (minor): 'Cramping' is an interpretation; udveṣṭana is literally 'twisting, wrapping round'.

old: उसे अभ्यक्त करके, धान्यों से स्वेदित करके, यष्टीमधु में पकाए हुए तेल से अनुवासन दे।
new: उसे अभ्यक्त करके, धान्यों से स्वेदित करके, यष्टीमधु से पकाए हुए तेल से अनुवासन दे।
why: reviewer (minor): 'में' (in) renders the instrumental of vipakka; elsewhere 'से सिद्ध/पकाए' is used. English says 'cooked with'.

old: जो स्निग्ध और स्विन्न है, जिसका कोष्ठ अत्यन्त मृदु है अथवा जो भूखा है, उसके लिए प्रयुक्त तीक्ष्ण वेग वाली अथवा बहुत अधिक औषध सब मल को निकालकर और धातुओं को भी द्रवीभूत करके बहा दे, तो वह अतियोगी होती है।
new: जो स्निग्ध और स्विन्न है, जिसका कोष्ठ अत्यन्त मृदु है अथवा जो भूखा है, उसके लिए प्रयुक्त तीक्ष्ण वेग वाला अथवा बहुत अधिक औषध सब मल को निकालकर और धातुओं को भी द्रवीभूत करके बहा दे; वह अतियोगी होता है।
why: reviewer (minor): (1) The added conditional 'तो' is not in the Sanskrit (the draft's own note admits this), so something is added. (2) औषध is masculine in Hindi and is made masculine in unit 48 ('औषध ... कुपित करता है'), but here it is treated as feminine (वाली, होती).

old: उसे सौ बार धोए हुए घृत से अभ्यक्त करके, कषाय, स्वादु और शीत द्रव्यों से, लेप, सेचन, अवगाहन, अन्न और पान के रूप में, और शर्करा तथा मधु वाले लेहों से स्तम्भित करे।
new: उसे सौ बार धोए हुए घृत से अभ्यक्त करके, कसैले, मीठे और शीतल द्रव्यों से, लेप, सेचन, अवगाहन, अन्न और पान के रूप में, और शर्करा तथा मधु वाले लेहों से स्तम्भित करे।
why: reviewer (error): kaṣāya is correctly the taste 'astringent' in this taste-list (kaṣāya-svādu-śīta qualifying the smearings, pourings, immersions, food and drink), and the English says so. But Hindi 'कषाय' reads as 'decoction' (काढ़ा) to a modern reader, and स्वादु reads as 'tasty'. So the Hindi gives a different sense from the English.

old: Having anointed him with ghṛta washed a hundred times, he should make him firm (stambhayet) with astringent, sweet and cold things, as smearing, pouring, immersion, food and drink, and with linctuses containing sugar and honey.
new: Having anointed him with ghṛta washed a hundred times, he should make him firm (stambhayet) with astringent, sweet and cold things, as smearing, pouring, immersion, food and drink, and with licked preparations (leha) containing sugar and honey.
why: reviewer (minor): 'Linctus' is a modern pharmacy word for a cough medicine and implies an effect; leha is literally 'licked (preparation)'.

old: with linctuses
new: with licked preparations
why: reviewer (minor): Same as above.

old: tat-puruṣa, n. acc. sg.
new: tat-puruṣa, n. nom. sg.
why: reviewer (minor): Both are labelled acc. sg., but the coordinated sarpiḥ-maṃḍaḥ is nominative, so the list is nominative with an elided copula (the draft's own anuvāsanam is n. nom. sg.). The case labels are inconsistent.

old: n. acc. sg.
new: n. nom. sg.
why: reviewer (minor): See above.

old: Construction is loose: the verb avacārayet (glossary: OPEN, literal 'should administer') may govern the whole list, or only the final 'milk cooked with binding substances at the meal'; the second reading is followed. mākṣika may be 'honey' or a mineral name; kept as mākṣika. kṣīrivṛkṣa kept as a name (milk-bearing trees), not identified.
new: Construction is loose: the verb avacārayet (glossary: OPEN, literal 'should administer') may govern the whole list, or only the final 'milk cooked with binding substances at the meal'; the translation follows the first reading (the verb governs the whole list). mākṣika may be 'honey' or a mineral name; kept as mākṣika. kṣīrivṛkṣa kept as a name (milk-bearing trees), not identified.
why: reviewer (minor): The note says the narrower reading (avacārayet governs only the last item) is followed, but both the English and the Hindi put the verb after the whole list and apply it to all items, i.e. the first reading. Note and translation disagree.

old: past part. √miśr, n. inst. sg.
new: adj. (miśra), n. inst. sg.
why: reviewer (minor): miśra is an adjective ('mixed'), not a past participle of a root √miśr.

old: निकले हुए गुद को अभ्यक्त करके, स्वेदित करके और कषायों से स्तम्भित करके भीतर प्रविष्ट कराए।
new: निकले हुए गुद को अभ्यक्त करके, स्वेदित करके और कसैले द्रव्यों से स्तम्भित करके भीतर प्रविष्ट कराए।
why: reviewer (minor): kaṣāyaiḥ is a bare plural noun here (no taste-list). English chose 'astringent things', but Hindi 'कषाय' reads as decoctions (काढ़ा), so the two languages differ on the sense. The sense is genuinely open (astringent substances or decoctions); at least the two languages must agree, and the unit's 'high' confidence overstates it.

new: jīvaraktapittayoḥ is read as a dvandva of jīvarakta ('life-blood') and (rakta)pitta, matching raktapitta in unit 74; the compound may have lost one rakta. ubhayatra 'in both' is presumably the two excesses (vamana and virecana) or the two blood-conditions treated above (raktapitta, raktātisāra); the text does not say.

new: jīvaraktapittayoḥ is read as a dvandva of jīvarakta ('life-blood') and (rakta)pitta, matching raktapitta in unit 74; the compound may have lost one rakta. ubhayatra 'in both' is presumably the two excesses (vamana and virecana) or the two blood-conditions treated above (raktapitta, raktātisāra); the text does not say.
